item.title: Family of bikini designer in Montauk yacht death files $50M lawsuit alleging assault
item.description: A wrongful death lawsuit alleges Christopher Durnan assaulted an Irish bikini designer aboard a yacht at Star Island Yacht Club in Montauk last August.
item.content:encoded:
The family of a bikini designer who was found dead on a Montauk yacht last summer has filed a $50 million lawsuit alleging assault in a case that rocked the wealthy summer hot spot.

"It's been very difficult for the family," said attorney Michael Bowe.

He is representing Martha Nolan-O’Slatarra's family in their recently filed wrongful death lawsuit alleging she was assaulted before her death.

Nolan-O’Slatarra was an Irish bikini designer living in New York City who was found dead aboard a luxury yacht in Montauk last summer. She founded East x East, a boutique resort wear label she frequently promoted through stylish behind-the-scenes glimpses of her photo shoots and design process.

IRISH BIKINI DESIGNER MARTHA NOLAN LAID TO REST IN IRELAND AS CAUSE OF DEATH REMAINS UNKNOWN

"The EMTs, when they arrived, found blood in her mouth. On her chest, on her head, and they believe behind her, behind her head," Bowe said.

Bowe's team filed a summons with notice against Christopher Durnan in Manhattan Supreme Court on Tuesday. The filing alleges Durnan "intentionally and wrongfully assaulted" Nolan-O’Slatarra aboard a vessel at the Star Island Yacht Club on or about Aug. 4 and Aug. 5, 2025.

Bowe said Nolan-O’Slatarra's family has endured both unbearable heartbreak and a grueling, year-long wait for answers.

"They've conducted their own investigation. We've been conducting our own investigation and it includes a second autopsy by the family by a well-renowned medical examiner, as well as other evidence that we have, some of which we've shared, some of we won't. And then obviously through the discovery process, we expect to secure all the evidence so it can be presented in court," he said.

WOMAN FOUND DEAD ON YACHT SPARKS SCRUTINY OF MONTAUK’S PARTY SCENE AND RISING WEALTH

The family's lawsuit accuses Durnan of gross negligence and reckless conduct that allegedly caused her injuries and death. The document does not describe the alleged assault or explain what happened aboard the yacht.

Bowe said Durnan has not made an effort to contact Nolan-O’Slatarra's family.

"He's made various public comments that simply aren't true. Like he's make public comments about how he's in communication with the family. The family reached out to him multiple times by phone and by text, as you would expect, and those overtures were never responded to," he said.

Her family is seeking damages for wrongful death, as well as for personal injuries and the conscious pain and suffering she allegedly experienced before she died.

The filing also seeks punitive damages, interest, attorneys’ fees and court costs.

item.title: Former NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom writes letter to WNBA officially declaring for 2027 draft
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom officially submitted his letter declaring for the 2027 WNBA Draft, citing league rules amid the Sophie Cunningham controversy.
item.content:encoded:
The wheels are in motion in the WNBA ... or they're falling off.

One or the other.

Former first-round NBA draft pick Enes Kanter Freedom has made good on his promise to declare for next year's WNBA Draft, officially penning a letter to the league on Monday.

THE WNBA HAS LIMITED OPTIONS AFTER TWO MEN DECLARED FOR THE DRAFT, AND THOSE OPTIONS AREN'T GREAT

Kanter shared the letter in a social media post, saying "rules are rules!" in the caption.

"Please accept this formal document as my official written notification to the Women's National Basketball Association of my voluntary decision to enter the player pool for the 2027 WNBA Draft," the letter said. "Consistent with the current league collective bargaining agreement, I am submitting this notice to exercise my draft rights and to affirm that I at least twenty-two years old and that I have no remaining intercollegiate eligibility, as required by Article XIII, Section 1(b).

"I request that the WNBA League Office verify receipt of this document and direct any future communications to my personal email address listed above. Thank you for your official processing of my registration into the 2027 draft pool."

What a time to be alive. What a league. More importantly, what a pickle for that league.

Kanter and former first round NBA pick, Royce White, both declared their intentions to enter the WNBA Draft late last week as a clear rebuttal to the ongoing drama surrounding Sophie Cunningham and the league.

Cunningham told ESPN last month that she believed in protecting young girls in sports.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" she told the outlet. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

Pretty simple statement, right? Wrong!

That reignited the "trans in women's sports" debate — which then led to several protests from both sides before Fever games. Earlier this month, Minnesota head coach Cheryl Reeve made her stance known by wearing a "Trans kids belong" shirt during a game against Cunningham and the Fever.

The WNBA has since come out with a boilerplate statement praising the "different lived experiences, cultures, lifestyles, and opinions" in the wake of the trans-athlete debate reaching the league.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"To everyone who loves this game: The WNBPA represents 200+ individual people with different lived experiences, cultures, lifestyles, and opinions. We embrace justice , equity, diversity, and inclusion. Those are the values that unite this Union and allow it to protect women's sports while creating transformational change," the league added.

"Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm. We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns."

Speaking of politics, Cunningham was fouled so violently over the weekend by Chicago Sky player DiJonai Carrington that she was ejected from the game, only to then post "White privilege" on social media from the locker room.

The league will now have to, presumably, make a decision today about whether Carrington should be suspended after being assessed a Flagrant 2.

After that, they'll have to dive into Kanter's letter.

Stay tuned.

item.title: Socialist leader squirms during TV interview when forced to address push to abolish prisons, police
item.description: A DSA leader on NBC Los Angeles dodged pointed questions about what happens to violent criminals if police and prisons are abolished as proposed.
item.content:encoded:
A socialist leader squirmed during a tense Sunday interview after a local California television anchor pressed her on the real-life ramifications of the radical party's calls to abolish police and prisons.

In an interview with NBC 4 Los Angeles, anchor Conan Nolan posed pointed questions to Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) National Political Committee Member Frances Gill on the topics of law enforcement, immigration and the movement's other far-left proposals.

After a brief back-and-forth over what defunding the police means and how that would be applied in practice, Gill resorted to deflecting by refusing to engage in 'hypotheticals.'

DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY'

"What we really want to see is a horizon where folks are not reliant on armed enforcement to meet our public safety needs," Gill conceded.

"Right, but it says 'defund police' on your website — that's your goal — and also to get rid of prisons and jails, correct?" he pressed, to which Gill answered affirmatively.

"So if my daughter is assaulted and raped, is there any agency that would seek to find her assailant and bring him to justice?" asked Nolan.

"Of course, yeah of course—" said Gill before the host jumped back in with a follow-up question.

"What would it be if not police and where would he be if not a jail?" asked Nolan.

SOCIALIST HOUSE NOMINEE'S RADICAL LAW-AND-ORDER VISION: 'WHAT ARE ILLEGALS?'

"So I guess I really want to avoid getting caught into these hypotheticals and talk about the reality that we're actually facing right now," Gill dodged.

That reality, she said, is the city spending "outrageous amounts on police and policing," instead of addressing real issues plaguing Los Angeles. She suggested that the lack of street lights, substance abuse treatment and mental healthcare are all contributing to a lack of public safety and rise in crime.

The pair then clashed over voter demographics in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, won by DSA-adjacent candidate Abdul El-Sayed — closely associated with extremist streamer Hasan Piker, who once said America deserved 9/11. The two palled around on the campaign trail.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Nolan noted that El-Sayed's support came overwhelmingly from college-educated voters like Gill, and that El-Sayed lost the state's 15 counties where the majority of voters did not have a college degree, characterizing the latter as the "working class" that DSA claims to support. Noting that she has $500,000 in student debt, Gill said college-educated voters like herself believed their degrees would lead to prosperity, but ultimately they found themselves downwardly mobile because society's "scales are tipped in one direction to benefit the rich."

On the issue of border security, Gill became defensive and questioned whether Nolan was acting in "good faith" when he quizzed her about whether there would be any border security if, like the DSA promotes, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) was abolished.

DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"I guess I don't understand why we kind of constantly get pinned on these particular questions when the immediate reality of the situation is that immigration enforcement is absolutely out of control, needs to be addressed immediately and we know that in Los Angeles, like, more than almost any other city in the country," she said.

She also denied that former President Joe Biden opened the borders. U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) data show that the agency encountered at least 11 million people during Biden's presidency.

Under President Donald Trump, that number has waned to fewer than 10,000 per month, and the administration touts that zero illegal aliens have been released into the country since retaking office.

Fox News Digital reached out to DSA for comment on Gill's interview.

item.title: Spencer Pratt praises fierce GOP foe in rare bipartisan turn: ‘Major props’
item.description: Spencer Pratt praised Adam Schiff and Rick Scott for passing the Doug LaMalfa Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act to help wildfire victims.
item.content:encoded:
Republican former Los Angeles mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt is giving rare praise to Democratic Sen. Adam Schiff after the California senator helped push through bipartisan disaster relief legislation benefiting wildfire victims like Pratt.

"Major props to [Sen. Adam Schiff] and [Sen. Rick Scott] for working across the aisle to get this done," Pratt wrote late last week. "Disaster recovery is hard enough as it is. A little bit of financial relief goes a long way. It’s easy to complain, but good leadership is very rare."

Pratt, who lost his home during the Palisades wildfire in 2025, was referencing the Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act, which the Senate passed on Aug. 7, sending it to President Donald Trump’s desk for approval.

KAREN BASS MEETS WITH TRUMP AT WHITE HOUSE TO PUSH FOR LA WILDFIRE RELIEF AFTER MONTHS OF CLASHES

Under current rules, in order for an individual to claim a disaster relief tax break, the damage to their property resulting from a federally declared disaster must meet or exceed 10% of their adjusted gross income. Someone who makes $100,000 per year, for instance, must incur $10,000 in damages before they can deduct the damages from their tax bill.

If the new disaster relief legislation is signed into law, that threshold would be removed for individuals who experienced disasters between December 28, 2019, and July 4, 2025, a period that covers the California wildfires, which destroyed the home of Pratt and many of Schiff’s other constituents.

OLD TRAILS FIRE SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY CONFESSED TO SETTING 25 FIRES; JUDGE DOUBLES BAIL TO $2M

"California politicians completely failed their residents after the fires. I flew to LA and met with [Pratt] at his burned-down lot. It was devastating," Scott said of the legislation, which he and Schiff sponsored. "After meeting with him, we fought to get this done. I appreciate all of Spencer’s work in helping us deliver much-needed relief for wildfire victims."

Additionally, the bill designates all wildfire relief payments as untaxable income. The 2025 California wildfires destroyed nearly 13,000 housing units and caused between $28.0 billion and $53.8 billion in damages, according to the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation.

EXCLUSIVE: WOMAN WHO STOLE $1.7M MEANT FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS GETS PRISON TIME AS DHS CRACKS DOWN ON FEMA FRAUD

The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office estimated that the Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act will result in the federal government losing $408 million in revenue between 2026 and 2036.

Pratt wasn’t the only Californian conservative to praise Schiff for his work to pass the disaster relief legislation.

"Thank you [Scott] and [Schiff] for seeing this through," James Johansson, a Republican farmer running for the California State Assembly, wrote on X. "With all that we’ve been through here in the North State we had no better champion and friend than [Rep. Doug LaMalfa]. Our friend is missed but leaves a big legacy for his constituents that won’t be forgotten."

LaMalfa, who the bill is named after, spent 13 years representing a northern California district in the House of Representatives, where he was an advocate for agricultural interests before dying in January following a heart-related medical emergency. He was known as an "affable, approachable and pragmatic lawmaker," according to The Washington Post.

Schiff’s office did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

item.title: Rangers vs Angels betting preview highlights Reid Detmers strikeout prop at +132 odds tonight
item.description: MacKenzie Gore and Reid Detmers face off as the Texas Rangers host the Los Angeles Angels, with a strikeout prop and MLB betting picks in play.
item.content:encoded:
If you haven't been following my baseball bets for the past few weeks, you've likely been missing out. Even when I'm not hitting a full game bet, I've been getting some good results with the player props we've taken. I'm not tooting my own horn here. I know the tide can turn at any moment, but you try to ride winning streaks and stretches as long as possible. I'm hoping to keep the good work coming here as the Rangers take on the Angels.

The Texas Rangers are looking for their path to the postseason. It is hard to say exactly how they can get there if it isn't by winning their division. I personally think the Wild Card race will be too cluttered for them to win it. Last year, the third Wild Card spot had a record of 87-75, and I don't see the Rangers getting to be 12 games over .500 this season. They currently sit at 59-59, which is even more remarkable considering they were 81-81 last year. So over their past 280 games, they are exactly .500.

Based on most of their stats, it seems like they are going to need pitching to lead the way. That was probably a fairly easy prediction at the beginning of the season when examining the roster. Today, they send out MacKenzie Gore to the hill. For the season, Gore is 6-9 with a 4.55 ERA and a 1.24 WHIP. Those aren't overly encouraging numbers, but he does have 140 strikeouts to go with it. He has made two starts against the Angels, and it has been a mixed bag. In the first outing, he allowed one earned run over six innings. Then last time, he allowed seven earned runs in five innings.

Texas Rangers Giving Away Blood-Stained Nolan Ryan Jerseys

The Los Angeles Angels, as usual, haven't had much go right this season and do not have a path to the playoffs. That may be an overstatement; they technically aren't eliminated, but they have the worst record in baseball. The team did make some decent moves at the trade deadline, but they were for the future, not things that will make a difference this year. They have an aggressive owner, but he mostly spends on guys who are headed toward the end of their careers.

One guy that the Angels kept, despite interest, was Reid Detmers and he takes the hill tonight. Detmers is just 27 years old, so he still should have some strong seasons ahead of him. I'm not sure where scouts view him, but I have him with a ceiling of being a number two starter. More likely, he will be a third guy on a playoff team. Detmers is 3-8 with a 4.12 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. He is 10th in the league in strikeouts with 150 of them this season. As long as he stays healthy, he will set a career high in strikeouts this season, and it will be his best WHIP ever and second-best ERA.

Detmers has very similar results to Gore. Against the Angels, he has had one good start and one rough one. In May, he went eight innings and allowed just one solo homer while striking out 14 hitters. The next time, Texas was ready for him. He allowed five earned runs in four innings. He did still have six strikeouts.

If I take a shot on this, it will be at a small amount. item.title: US State Department has yanked more than 175k visas under Trump administration so far
item.description: The U.S. State Department announced that more than 175,000 visas have been revoked under President Donald Trump's administration so far.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The U.S. State Department announced on Monday that it has revoked more than 175,000 visas during President Donald Trump's administration so far.

The announcement comes less than two years since Trump started his second term.

"Under President Trump, the United States Department of State has revoked more than 175,000 visas from foreign nationals who violated the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against U.S. citizens, defrauded Americans, abused our immigration system, or endangered national security," the State Department noted.

FOREIGN DRUNK DRIVERS COULD FACE SWIFT BOOT OUT OF COUNTRY UNDER TRUMP'S 'AMERICA FIRST' CRACKDOWN

"The majority of these visas were revoked due to law enforcement encounters for a range of criminal activity, with assault, driving under the influence, theft, and drug crimes being the leading causes. A significant share of visas were revoked for reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse, fraud and embezzlement, and other crimes," according to the department.

The department pointed to some examples of individuals who allegedly committed heinous crimes.

TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDERS TARGETING BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP, BIRTH TOURISM AFTER SUPREME COURT SETBACK

It indicated some of the individuals whose visas were revoked included "A foreign national who was charged with felony rape and sexual battery – including of a victim who was mentally disabled" and "A foreign national charged with felony kidnapping, human trafficking, and sexual exploitation of a minor."

The department also pointed to the issue of birth tourism.

"A U.S. embassy in North Africa revoked over 100 visas for 'birth tourist' parents who came to the United States primarily to give birth so their children would get U.S. citizenship," the department noted.

TRUMP ADMIN REVOKES BRAZILIAN AMBASSADOR'S VISA IN ESCALATING DIPLOMATIC FEUD

"Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, the State Department will continue to identify, investigate, and revoke the visas of foreign nationals who threaten the safety of the American people. A U.S. visa is a privilege, not a right. The Department remains committed to using every tool available to protect our communities from those who abuse it," the department declared.

Fox News' Nicholas Kalman contributed to this report.

item.title: Darline Graham details how she'd forge own path in Senate while carrying on brother Lindsey's legacy
item.description: Darline Graham says she shares South Carolina families' struggles with gas, groceries and healthcare as she campaigns ahead of Tuesday's special election.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., isn't trying to be a carbon copy of her late brother Lindsey, but as she vies for the opportunity to fill his Senate seat long-term, she's determined to carry on his legacy while forging a path of her own.

"I think Lindsey was an amazing senator," she said Monday on "Fox & Friends."

"His interest was foreign relations and national security, as we know. And while national security is really important, I'm a little different..."

SEN DARLINE GRAHAM REVEALS WHETHER SHE WILL RUN FOR A FULL-TERM DURING ‘HANNITY’ EXCLUSIVE

Lindsey Graham spent decades carving out a reputation as one of the Senate's leading foreign policy hawks. His sister, now South Carolina's junior senator, says her focus would be closer to home — particularly on the financial pressures facing families across the state.

"I want to focus on the struggles of the South Carolina families because, like them, I feel those same struggles," she shared.

Graham said voters on the campaign trail have repeatedly raised concerns about affordability, including the cost of gas, groceries and healthcare. In a last-minute pitch ahead of Tuesday's special election, she pointed to her two daughters' serious health issues and her own bargain-shopping habits as examples of how those pressures have hit home.

"I struggle, too... when I go shopping, I'm a bargain shopper," she said.

MACE SNUBS TRUMP'S PREFERRED SENATE CANDIDATE, BACKS RALPH NORMAN INSTEAD

"If the steak's not on sale, I don't buy it that week. I look for the buy one, get one free sale, so I think, like most South Carolinians, I live the struggles here, too, and we have to get the economy booming and cut government spending in order to get the prices down."

Graham is among ten Republicans vying for voters' support in Tuesday's election, capping a whirlwind stretch that thrust her into the political arena following her brother's sudden death in July.

She acknowledged the toll of simultaneously grieving Lindsey, adjusting to life in the Senate and mounting a campaign to keep the seat long-term.

"Over the past three weeks, I've buried my precious brother. I've learned the new role in the United States Senate. I'm on this brutal campaign trail with a brutal schedule," she said.

item.title: Incredible Michael Block drama, young American streak continues on PGA Tour and Joaquin Niemann does it again
item.description: Michael Brennan fired a final round 64 to win the Wyndham Championship by three shots, extending a young American winning streak on the PGA Tour.
item.content:encoded:
Go ahead and tell everyone you know that American golf is officially on the up and up.

The final three events on the PGA Tour schedule always feel like a slog given the weak-ish fields and being bookended by The Open and the start of the FedEx Cup Playoffs, but all three being won by an American under the age of 25 made for a mighty enjoyable close to the regular season.

Michael Brennan was the man responsible for extending the young American streak to three with his victory at the Wyndham Championship, and did so in style with a final round 64.

Over in Scotland, Michael Block did some things during the final round of the Staysure PGA Seniors Championship. It's preposterous that Block is making headlines in August 2026 while playing on the European Senior Tour, but it would be downright irresponsible not to break down what may (or may not) have transpired with the king of content across the pond.

Joaquin Niemann won another LIV Golf event, bringing his total to nine titles on the breakaway circuit. He officially has as many LIV wins as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau do, combined.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you need to know. You can follow Mark on X @itismarkharris and email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

First it was 21-year-old Jackson Koivun winning the 3M Open, then it was 24-year-old Michael Thorbjornsen taking home the Rocket Classic, and this week Brennan wins the Wyndham Championship by three shots for his second win on Tour at the age of 24 as well. It's objectively fun, if you're American that is, to see the final three tournaments of the PGA Tour regular season get picked off by three Americans in the infant stages of their careers.

Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker spoke early last week about his strategy when it comes to making his six captain's picks for the September event, stressing that he wasn't going to select young players for the sake of it, but what we've witnessed over the last three weeks he may be left with no other choice. Strong runs from any of these three players - or other youngsters in the conversation - throughout the playoffs is going to make things mighty interesting.

When it comes to Brennan's performance on Sunday afternoon, it was just about as good as it gets when beginning the day tied for the lead and in the final pairing.

After settling into the round with three pars to start the day, he opted to put his foot on the gas beginning on the Par 4 fourth hole and rattled off five straight birdies. It's probably not fair to say it was cruise control from that point onward with 10 holes left between winning a second win on Tour, but that's certainly what it felt like with Brennan in control of his golf swing and 54-hole co-leader Beau Hossler searching for most of the day.

Brennan's biggest weapon in the bag is the driver, and he had it working throughout the week, finishing ninth in average driving distance and third in strokes gained: off the tee. He falls into that category of player where if the putter gets scorching hot, he's likely going to find his way onto the first page of the leaderboard in a weaker field event like the Wyndham. Seeing as how he picked up nearly nine shots on the field with the flatstick for the week, the putter was insanely warm.

Brennan's victory at the Wyndham earns him an invitation back to next year's Masters, and his mother delivering that news while celebrating on the 18th green made for a fantastic moment.

Do with this information what you will, but Michael Brennan now has as many wins on the PGA Tour as Ludvig Aberg.

For anyone who may have forgotten about Michael Block, which, first of all, how dare you, but he is the PGA professional who took over the 2023 PGA Championship, finishing T-15, hitting a hole-in-one while playing with Rory McIlroy, and becoming one of the most memable and quotable characters the game has ever seen.

Despite his moment in the spotlight coming over three years ago, Block has remained a topic of conversation by qualifying for each of the last three PGA Championships, getting into the YouTube golf space, and receiving sponsor's exemptions into tournaments here and there.

Speaking of sponsor's exemptions, Block received one to compete in this week's Staysure PGA Seniors Championship, which is a European Senior Tour event in Scotland not even televised in the United States, but Blockie still found a way to get us to pay attention.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Ryan French, better known in the golf world as Monday Q Info, shared on X on Sunday afternoon that people he had spoken to explained that Block withdrew during the final round after the 12th hole and simply walked off the golf course without saying anything to his playing partners.

A bizarre alleged move, but one that wouldn't be all that surprising coming from the character that is Mr. Block.

On top of that, it was reported that Block showed up to his final round tee time late and was given a two-stroke penalty.

Showing up late to a tee time and then quitting with six holes to go, while you're there playing on a sponsor's exemption, is truly unbelievable, yet things somehow got even more ridiculous when Block chimed in on social media.

After French's reporting caught fire on social media, Block jumped on Instagram and posted a statement in which he confirmed he was "a couple of seconds late" to his tee time on Sunday because he "got caught up taking pictures for volunteers" before admitting it was "completely my fault."

Playing victim while in the tournament on a freebie, trying to cast yourself as the good guy in the situation, is both condescending and objectively hilarious.

Evin Priest of Golf Digest managed to get a hold of Block via text message on Sunday, to which he actually confirmed he was technically disqualified from the tournament, did tell his partners he was calling it quits, but also explained that he picked up a wrist injury while hitting a shot from a bush on the 10th hole.

The Legends Tour issued its own statement confirming Block had been disqualified after leaving the course before "completing his round and without completing the necessary process of advising tour officials of any injury or illness."

So, nobody knew of the apparent wrist injury other than Block, who shared the information hours after French's reporting and didn't feel obliged to disclose the information on his own social media when explaining the situation.

Convenient is the first word that comes to mind.

Joaquin Niemann won this week's LIV event. Some iteration of that sentence has now been written nine times since he left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2022. To further put into perspective how great Niemann has been on the LIV circuit in recent years, he didn't pick up his first win until February 2024. Nine wins across the span of 30 months isn't too shabby.

Niemann's win over the weekend came at Trump Bedminster, where he secured a three-shot margin over Harold Varner III. He also beat Bryson DeChambeau by a smooth 23 shots, with the two-time U.S. Open champion putting together his worst performance in years.

Niemann, who is still just 27 years old, has now earned over $80 million in on-course earnings alone since joining LIV Golf, which is a nice chunk of change to throw on top of the reported nine-figure deal he signed to begin with.

Nobody has come close to benefiting more with a move to LIV than Niemann. Yes, his major championship history is still bad with just two Top 15 finishes in 29 starts, but nine wins, which is four more than any other LIV player, is undeniably impressive.

item.title: El-Sayed admits free healthcare means paying 'a little bit more in taxes' regardless of income
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed appeared to acknowledge on NBC's "Meet the Press" that Americans would pay more in taxes under his Medicare for All plan for the Senate.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed appeared to admit on Sunday's "Meet the Press" that everyone, regardless of income, would have to pay "a little bit more in taxes" for universal healthcare.

NBC News host Kristen Welker asked El-Sayed about his support for Medicare for All and whether Americans need to worry about paying more taxes to make it possible.

El-Sayed answered that he was in favor of raising taxes on billionaires but seemed to concede that even Americans earning under $1 million or less would also see their taxes increase.

FETTERMAN 'DARES' EL-SAYED TO STICK WITH PIKER, CLAIMS MICHIGAN NOMINEE HAS 'LITTLE MAN SYNDROME ENERGY'

"So, for the average person, when you look at your W2, if you’re an employee who gets paid every two weeks or four weeks, after you pay your taxes, the next biggest check that comes off the top of your pay stub is to your health insurance company," El-Sayed answered. 

El-Sayed went on to describe what this would look like in action. 

"So imagine, instead of paying that to your health insurance company, whose CEO makes $20 million a year, instead, you paid a little bit more in taxes for healthcare that you wouldn’t lose if you lost your job or turned 26 or got married or got divorced. I think all of us would be a lot more interested in that kind of a system if we knew that our healthcare would be free at the point of care and would be free without having to worry about losing it, in general," he said. 

He continued, "So there’s an opportunity here, I think, to trade what we give to a big corporation, who gets to decide who we get to see and who we don’t, for a little bit more paid into FICA. And I think that’s a trade that’s worth making."

‘SPECIAL SAUCE OF CRAZY’ — MIDWEST DEM CANDIDATE’S POLICIES TOO EXTREME FOR VOTERS: OPPONENT

Welker questioned if this meant taxes would go up for anyone who wasn't a millionaire. 

"Just to be very clear, you’re describing this trade-off. You are effectively acknowledging that people making less than a million dollars could see their taxes go up. I just want to be very clear. Is that a yes?" Welker asked.

"I’m saying that we’d be paying for healthcare in a different way. Instead of paying a health insurance company, whose CEO makes $20 million, I would much rather pay for durable healthcare into a government, which, of course, we all know provides healthcare for seniors who need healthcare the most. So, if I’m trading paying a CEO to make more money or paying a government to guarantee me healthcare, I’m picking the latter every time," El-Sayed said.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment but did not immediately hear back.

El-Sayed's GOP opponent, Mike Rogers, commented on the interview on X, denouncing El-Sayed's proposal as more money for the government.

HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED'

"Weird. I thought Abdul’s campaign promise was more money in your pocket. This sounds a lot like more money for the government," Rogers wrote.

On Monday, Abdul responded to Rogers' post, saying, "I know it’s complicated for you, habibi. I’m happy to teach you how this works at our next debate…if you’re not too much a coward to debate me."

El-Sayed defeated establishment-backed candidate Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary last week after facing several controversies for campaigning with far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker.

Though El-Sayed supports policies like Medicare for All and taxing billionaires, he has insisted that he was not a socialist and did not endorse every position within the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). 

However, longtime Democrats, like former Hillary Clinton campaign strategist Julian Epstein, have viewed El-Sayed's ascension as a further sign that the Democratic Party is "off the deep end."

"The Democrats have gone off the deep end," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "I think the lunatics are in charge of the asylum. I think that there is no room in the tent for people that want to destroy our Constitution. There's no room in the tent for people that want to align themselves with radical Islam. There's no room in a tent for people that want to align themselves with antisemitism."

Political analyst Eric Ham said El-Sayed's victory in the primary is part of a broader battle over control of the Democratic Party itself.

"The ongoing battle between the establishment and DSA is about control of the party itself. In fact, DSA's primary target is not Trump or even taking back power in Washington," Ham told Fox News Digital. 

"Their main objective is to wrest control of the Party. As evidence, look no further than Mamdani's support of two progressive Dems to unseat incumbent lawmakers; El Sayed's upstart victory in Michigan against an incumbent who polled better against [Mike] Rogers; or even [Cori] Bush who attempted to win her seat back against an establishment lawmaker that defeated her," he said. 

"This attempted coup will continue through 2028 even if it means costing Dems the White House. DSA wants to win but on their terms and right now the focus is internal," Ham said.

item.title: Johnson turns Democrats’ socialist civil war into new weapon for midterms
item.description: House Republicans launch "Contrast for America" website targeting DSA-linked Democrats, echoing the 1994 "Contract with America" midterm strategy.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: House Republicans have adopted a new weapon on the campaign trail as they fight to keep control of Congress for the latter half of President Donald Trump's term — using Democrats' own intraparty civil war against them.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., is unveiling a website on Monday that will highlight the contrast between what he calls "common sense and crazy."

The name for the new initiative is "Contrast for America," a play on the Newt Gingrich-led "Contract with America" GOP policy platform used during the 1994 midterm election.

That same year saw a massive red wave help the GOP retake the House and Senate for the latter two years of former President Bill Clinton's first term, and Republicans are hoping to harness that energy now as they fight an uphill battle to retain the House and Senate.

MIKE JOHNSON PREDICTS GOP COULD GAIN UP TO EIGHT SEATS IN MIDTERMS, DEFYING HISTORICAL TRENDS

The website is divided into five separate parts, beginning with a video message from Johnson that includes a montage of Fox News clips and compares images of unrest in U.S. cities to videos of patriotic displays of the country's 250th anniversary.

"Freedom is never more than one generation away from extinction. It must be fought for. It must be protected. It has to be taught, passed along to the next generation. Thirty-five years ago, Republicans and Democrats in Congress, they were fighting communism on a distant shore. Now it's here," Johnson says in the video.

The website also includes a timeline of failed communist governments throughout the world, followed by dueling lists that show what Republicans are running on versus what Democrats' far-left insurgency is pushing.

SOCIALIST VICTORIES SHOW DEMS' DESCENT DOWN 'DEADLY PATH OF COMMUNISM,' JOHNSON WARNS

It comes as candidates linked to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) surge to the top of Democratic primaries across the United States, even toppling establishment and progressive incumbents in places like Colorado and New York.

Johnson's website highlights those specific DSA-linked candidates along with Republicans who are endorsed by House GOP leaders.

"House Republicans have delivered working families tax cuts to put more money in your pocket, a secure border, safer streets, American energy dominance, an end to woke indoctrination for our kids, and renewed American strength abroad. Meanwhile, Democrats have surrendered to the socialist and communist far-left that wants to abolish borders, defund police, abolish prisons, raise your taxes, and shred our Constitution, leaving America less safe, less prosperous, and less free," Johnson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"By highlighting this decisive contrast for America and our common sense polices and America first candidates, House Republicans are ready to defy history and win the midterms."

100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY

Political history shows that the party in power in the White House usually loses one or both houses of Congress during the midterm elections.

But the slate of DSA victories is giving Republicans new hope that they can buck tradition.

Among the DSA's policy goals are abolishing the Senate, police, and the prison system, extending voting rights to noncitizen permanent residents, and establishing public ownership of large corporations.

DSA candidates have also called for abolishing the nation's borders and granting mass amnesty to people in the U.S. illegally.

It's a message Johnson has made on the campaign trail already as he's campaigned in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Washington, Oregon, and Alaska, with plans to hit a total of 30 districts across 18 states.

Whether the message is potent enough to buck decades of political history, however, will become clear in November.

item.title: Battleground Dem called patriotism 'sensitive and controversial' during debate over the Pledge of Allegiance
item.description: Iowa Democrat Christina Bohannan called patriotism "sensitive and controversial" in a 2021 newsletter now resurfacing in her swing-district rematch.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: An Iowa Democrat seeking to flip one of the nation's most competitive House seats in a rematch described patriotism as "sensitive and controversial" while also questioning the meaning of the Pledge of Allegiance in a recently resurfaced newsletter she published in the weeks after the January 6 Capitol riot.

Former Iowa State Rep. Christina Bohannan of Iowa City, who is running against incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, R-Iowa, also criticized the politics around an Iowa bill she ultimately supported that mandated the Pledge of Allegiance for schoolchildren, urging Iowans to think critically about what the pledge means.

"I acknowledge that patriotism is a sensitive and controversial subject," Bohannan wrote in a 2021 newsletter put out by her State House office, while saying she remains patriotic herself.

DEMS PUT ON BLAST OVER POLL THAT SHOWS RECORD-LOW PATRIOTISM IN US: 'TEAR OUR SOCIETY APART'

"Many progressives have turned away from it. And I see the point, especially when the concept of patriotism has been so co-opted and distorted by the other side," she wrote of Republicans.

The newsletter has resurfaced as recent polling shows a partisan divide over displays of patriotism. AP polling released in June found that about six in 10 Democrats and independents said they never fly the American flag, while roughly seven in 10 Republicans said they display it at least on holidays.

Bohannan wrote that the right viewpoint is to "not cede patriotism to anyone" but instead restore its definition as a belief in "democratic ideals of America and a willingness to fight to make those ideals a reality."

Bohannan went on to critique a February 2021 Republican-led bill, which ultimately passed, requiring the recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance in public and certain private schools.

Bohannan's campaign manager, Dan Driscoll, told Fox News Digital that "Christina absolutely stands by her vote to require the Pledge of Allegiance in Iowa schools and her passionate defense of patriotism and the greatness of our country and democracy."

"That's why in Congress she'll put that into action by fighting to clean up Washington, enacting term limits and getting corporate money out of our elections, so our government focuses on working for Iowans — unlike Rep. Miller-Meeks who is funded by millions in special interest contributions while voting to raise drug, healthcare and energy costs."

FOX NEWS POLL: LOOKING AHEAD TO AMERICA'S 250TH ANNIVERSARY

The bill passed 91-3-6 with Bohannan in favor, but she wrote about her reservations in the same newsletter.

"It was clear that many of our Democratic members in swing districts would risk their seats for voting ‘no’ on this bill," Bohannan wrote. "And even if those members voted for it, they would still be held accountable if other members of our caucus voted ‘no’. That is how deep the concept of patriotism runs."

"But we can reframe the issue in a way that is true to our values."

IOWA DEM ADMITS BEING ‘UNCOMFORTABLE’ WITH WHITENESS AS SHE SEEKS TO FLIP COMPETITIVE HOUSE SEAT

Bohannan said in floor remarks at the time that she supported the bill not because she wanted children to "mechanically" recite the oath but because she wanted to give them the opportunity to "think critically" about the words they are saying and whether the U.S. is "living up to them."

"For example, the pledge is not just to the flag, but to the republic for which it stands. So our kids might ask whether our republic can last when our leaders fail to denounce those who subvert our democracy."

Miller-Meeks, a retired Army lieutenant colonel and medic, told Fox News Digital that patriotism "has never been controversial to me, not in the 24 years I served this country and not now."

"Bohannan and her DSA allies are free to call loving America ‘controversial,’ but they have no business representing Iowa," Miller-Meeks said.

Zach Kraft, a spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said Bohannan’s comments were predictable in light of prior controversial support she offered for the left-wing pro-DEI "1619 Project."

'QUEEN OF DEI' RUNNING FOR CONGRESS RIPPED HER RURAL STATE AS 'BACKWARDS' ON PODCAST

"Leave it to the Queen of DEI to hate America," Kraft told Fox News Digital.

"Only a true... woke warrior like Christina Bohannan could find patriotism offensive but see nothing wrong with calling Iowans backwards for believing in basic biology."

Bohannan warned against a bill prohibiting diversity and "implicit bias" training at schools and universities statewide, calling the Hawkeye State potentially "backward" if it passed.

BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT FLIP-FLOPS ON CONVERSION THERAPY AFTER LEFT-WING BACKLASH

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think that it is going to be very divisive if passed. I think that it's going to send a very bad message about Iowa and that it is going to seem like are kind of this backwards state that doesn't understand there are things like systemic racism."

Miller-Meeks previously defeated Bohannan by about six percentage points in 2022, but the Democrat narrowly lost in 2024 in a race that triggered a recount and resulted in the Republican being re-elected by about 800 votes.

The district, which includes Davenport and Iowa City, home to the University of Iowa, is competing with Rep. Zach Nunn's district to the west for the distinction of being the most competitive in the state.

More importantly, the date will also change, and it's maybe the smartest thing NASCAR's done in a while.

The 2027 Wheatley Vodka Clash (yes, it's no longer the Busch Clash) will run Saturday night, Feb. 13 — eight days before the Daytona 500 and on the eve of the Super Bowl.

Yes, you read that right. We finally get some iteration of "Speedweeks" back. The horrible "run the Busch Clash then take a full two weeks off before the Daytona 500" schedule is DONE. One of the dumbest scheduling strategies in all of sports, if you ask me, and it's finally over.

The race will run on the oval, with eligibility for the invitation-only event still to be determined. The late Kyle Busch won the last Clash at Daytona in 2021, but that race was on the road course.

Yes, Kyle Busch won a road course race. Amazing. Man, I miss him.

Look at that schedule. What a throwback! In recent years, the old "Speedweeks" have turned into "SpeedDays," with some drivers not even getting to Daytona until the Wednesday before the race.

Disgusting behavior, if you ask me. Not anymore.

We've got the Clash a full eight days before the 500, and a on the eve of the Super Bowl. Another smart move. The Super Bowl is a full week later this year, which means the 500 has been pushed a week. NASCAR made the right call jamming a race into Super Bowl weekend. You get a piece of that pie however possible. Trust me.

Good to have some sort of Speedweeks back. Lord, I'm just glad to have it plural again.

OK, that's enough of the warm and fuzzy today. Unfortunately, I can't milk it forever. Everyone's favorite Aussie announcer, Leigh Diffey, returned to our TV screens this weekend, and NASCAR fans were thrilled!

I could go on and on, but I won't, because I'm tired. We've been doing this song and dance with Leigh Diffey for five years now it seems.

Look, I don't love him, but I've made peace with him. Does it sound different? Yeah, duh. Let's just be honest here for a second. It sounds like I should be watching an F1 race, and Lord knows I'd never watch an F1 race.

But credit to Leigh for at least trying to make yesterday's race sound exciting. It's not an easy job, you know? Try to make a race with these current cars, which don't allow you to pass, sound exciting.

It ain't easy. Mike Joy does it better than anyone (duh), but I thought Leigh was fine yesterday. He did at one point call the final few laps "phenomenal," which I guess were? I don't know. Did anyone think Christopher Bell would actually pass Ty Gibbs? You couldn't do it all day. Why would it happen at the end?

I will say this ... Leigh can make paint drying sound exciting. NASCAR fans will never get past the accent, which I get, but fair is fair.

OK, let's get to a couple quickies on the way to Richmond ... First? How about this Kyle Busch helmet Ryan Blaney broke out this weekend?

"My thought when Kyle passed was, I've always thought in situations like that, how do you remember somebody and how do you think of all the good that they did in their life and all the success they had? Blaney said. "I think helmets are a unique thing in our sport, we kind of get to design them, a lot of them have special meaning. And this is kind of my best way of showing my respect towards Kyle Busch and respect to the Busch family.

"I hope to run it for one race and give it to Brexton, the Busch family, and they can do whatever they want with it. So just showing respect, and I'm glad people noticed it."

NASCAR DRIVER ALEX BOWMAN ANNOUNCES PLAN TO RETIRE FROM FULL-TIME COMPETITION AFTER 2027

Solid helmet out of Ryan Blaney yesterday. Well done. My favorite Kyle Busch win came in 2021 when he won the season-opening Clash because Chase Elliott wrecked Ryan Blaney.

Not really. But it was a cool win:

Can't believe it's been five years since NASCAR raced on Daytona's road course. Let's never do that again!

Speaking of Chase Elliott ... has anyone seen just how bad Hendrick Motorsports has been lately? Goodness gracious. This might be their worst summer ever, and that's saying a lot given they've historically had rough summer months.

William Byron finished ninth yesterday, giving HMS its first top-10 in nearly a month. Chase hasn't finished in the top-10 since Nashville ... on May 31!

Do you understand how bad that is? What in the world is going on over there?

Yikes.

OK, that's it for today. We made wine out of water. Or something like that.

Here's McCall Gaulding's vacation recap to take us to Richmond.

item.title: BROOKE ROLLINS, DR. BEN CARSON: We are putting real food back on school lunch trays
item.description: Trump administration's Make America Healthy Again initiative brings whole milk back to schools and awards $20 million in farm to school grants.
item.content:encoded:
America has long been known as a land of opportunity. It’s a place where every child, no matter where they were born or the circumstances they face, has the chance to chase their God-given potential. Whether you grew up on a farm in rural Texas or in the inner city of Detroit, America is a place that has always shown that with hard work, determination and the freedom to dream, there is no limit to what a person can achieve.

But along the way, there are certain habits that fuel our endurance or restrain it. And a big contributor to how effectively we can chase those dreams is our health.

In recent years, it’s no secret that America has been battling a chronic health crisis. The Centers for Disease Control reports that more than 75% of adults in the U.S. have at least one chronic health condition. And a recent study indicates poor health trends among children have worsened significantly over the past 20 years. The data shows that poor nutrition is among the causes of these startling health statistics.

STEAK 'N SHAKE'S NEW 'CHIEF MAHA OFFICER' TEASES RFK JR-INSPIRED MENU SHIFT

But there is good news — the Trump administration is working to change this trend. We know that good health starts with good nutrition, so to springboard the effort to Make America Healthy Again, USDA and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services jointly introduced the 2025–2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans earlier this year.

Relying on gold standard science, the Dietary Guidelines translate decades of nutrition research into practical recommendations that promote health across every stage of life.

The goal is simple: eat real food. It is well known that highly processed sugary foods can make the body feel sluggish and sick. Although they feed cravings, they don’t do much for the development of growing minds and bodies. On the other hand, whole, nutrient-dense foods are minimally processed and provide nourishment and the real fuel that growing kids need.

That’s why the Trump administration is partnering with states and local school districts to implement innovative ways to get whole, nutrient-dense foods to our kids. Through the State Early Action Pledge, states and local school districts across the country are voluntarily implementing one or more of the healthy options outlined in the updated Dietary Guidelines in the new school year — including serving whole milk to kids for the first time in more than a decade!

PALEO DIET LEADER BANS 'CAVEMAN' LABEL, SAYS HEALTHY EATING PLAN WIDELY MISUNDERSTOOD

Of course, America’s farmers and ranchers are also an essential part of feeding flourishing families. Every healthy school meal begins with the hardworking producers who grow our fruits, vegetables, grains, dairy products and protein. By strengthening the connection between schools and local agriculture, we support both children’s health and rural economies.

USDA’s Farm to School Grant Program, which awarded two cohorts totaling nearly $20 million in the last three months, connects farmers to children by incorporating local foods into school meals, summer meals and childcare settings.

This year, we implemented several improvements designed to streamline the grant application process, remove barriers, promote larger-scale partnerships and empower farm-to-school programs to achieve bigger, bolder goals on behalf of our children.

For example, for its Powered by Protein project, first-time grantee Foundation for Food and Farm Connections will partner with 10 school districts, a large food service company, the Missouri Farm Bureau and the Missouri Association of Meat Producers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

This project will help schools to source local beef, pork, and poultry by strengthening every link in the farm-to-farschool supply chain — from producers and processors to school nutrition staff and classrooms.

These exciting new projects and partnerships prove that healthy school meals are about far more than what appears on a lunch tray. They represent an investment in the future of our great nation. They strengthen American agriculture by creating reliable markets for farmers and ranchers. They support local communities by bringing schools, families and producers together around a common purpose. And they demonstrate what has been common sense all along: good nutrition and strong agriculture go hand in hand.

Benjamin S. Carson Sr., M.D. was the 17th secretary of the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development. He is the founder and chairman of the American Cornerstone Institute and an Emeritus Professor of Neurosurgery at Johns Hopkins Medicine.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan, returning after serious car crash, has new perspective on Tesla Autopilot and concussions
item.description: Kyle Shanahan reveals he still suffers headaches and fatigue from his concussion but will return to the 49ers sideline for Thursday's preseason opener.
item.content:encoded:
At his first press conference since causing a car crash that left him with broken ribs, a broken nose, a broken left hand, facial lacerations and a concussion, San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan announced he'll return to the sideline for his team's first preseason game this week.

But Shanahan wasn't done announcing.

He also made it clear his head-on collision in July, for which he's taken responsibility, has left him with a new perspective on Tesla's autopilot feature that seemingly drives the car by itself, and concussions, which are a significant part of all NFL seasons.

NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK

"When you're going at 20 miles an hour, and you're on autopilot, I honestly have zero worries," Shanahan told reporters. "I have so much trust in that stuff. That was a good lesson that you can't ever have zero worries. I think it definitely could be an example for a lot of people."

Shanahan is not a Tesla hater. He didn't protest the brand or Elon Musk back in 2025. In fact, he's owned Teslas for years.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

But this crash has made him see his driving experience differently.

"Dropping a phone, it falling all the way to my back seat to where I have to fully take my eyes off the road, it's something that I normally wouldn’t do," Shanahan said. "I've had autopilot for nine years, so I'm pretty comfortable with it. Who knows what happened when I turned around. Whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off, that's something I don't know yet.

"But regardless, it is always your fault, whether you're on autopilot or not. You can't take your eyes off the road. It's a partnership driving. You don't just turn it over to a computer. It's a good lesson, no matter how comfortable I am with that, that I believe someday could save my life or someone else's. It's really helped me have perspective on that stuff."

Shanahan hasn't been coaching the Niners at the outset of training camp to the degree he normally would. Even now, with the stitches on his face finally out, and Thursday's preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans looming, he's still walking around with a cast and some lingering effects of the crash.

And that has led him to view his players' concussions in a different light.

Shanahan, like many NFL coaches, is not intimately involved in the journey of his players through the league's concussion protocol. They do not determine when a player is cleared to return to practice or games.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But now, Shanahan admits, he "no doubt" has a new perspective on concussions.

"Just little things, like when they label things, like whether it's severe or mild," he said. "You hear someone has a mild one, I'm like, ‘Oh, alright. It might be one game, but usually that's two.’ Then you kind of learn those are just words. Each one's a little bit different.

"I definitely can relate to how scary it is when you don't know if you will feel right again. It's definitely made me more educated on it. Usually I just listen, and like, ‘Tell me when, OK,’ and I move on. But I understand it a lot better and what guys got to go through the protocol to get back."

Shanahan admits he's still not 100% following his concussion. He reports he still experiences headaches and fatigue.

Noise, particularly the soundtrack played over loudspeakers at practice, is no longer the challenge it was earlier.

"AC/DC hurt a lot more than some smoother hip-hop, but I think those days are over," he said. "Noise doesn't bother me like it was. I actually have two symptoms, I feel like, and that's headaches and fatigue. That's all I'm feeling right now."

Bieber's slideshow included a selfie in which she was seen posing in front of a mirror while rocking a skimpy two-piece that featured a gathered triangle top and matching low-rise bottoms that tied at the hips.

In another image, Bieber was clad in a blue and red tank top with blue and black cropped sweatpants as she laid on a patch of grass and flashed a bright smile. Bieber launched Rhode in June 2022 with three products: the Peptide Glazing Fluid, the Barrier Restore Cream and the Peptide Lip Treatment. As the brand grew in popularity, she went on to release other makeup and skincare products.

Rhode was acquired by e.l.f. in May 2025 in a deal valued at up to $1 billion, with Bieber staying on as chief creative officer and head of innovation.

"When I launched @rhode in 2022, I always had big dreams for the company, and the most important thing to me is to keep bringing rhode to more spaces, places, and faces globally," she announced on Instagram. "So today I am so incredibly excited and proud to announce that we are partnering with e.l.f. Beauty as we step into this next chapter in the world of rhode."

In May, Bieber became the global digital ambassador for the Italian swimwear label Calzedonia and starred in its summer 2026 campaign. During an interview with Elle magazine, Bieber shared her top swimwear styling tip.

"The fit is the most important part. Fit is everything," Bieber said.
